text:
Predicates:
NiceToAnimals(x) ::: x is nice to animals.
MeanToAnimals(x) ::: x is mean to animals.
Grumpy(x) ::: x is grumpy.
AnimalLover(x) ::: x loves animals.
OwnsPet(x) ::: x owns a pet.
LoveAnimals(x) ::: x loves animals.
Premises:
¬(NiceToAnimals(x) ∧ MeanToAnimals(x)) ::: No one who is nice to animals is mean to animals.
∃x (Grumpy(x) ∧ MeanToAnimals(x)) ::: Some grumpy people are mean to animals.
∀x (AnimalLover(x) → NiceToAnimals(x)) ::: All animal lovers are nice to animals.
∀x (OwnsPet(x) → LoveAnimals(x)) ::: If someone owns a pet, then they love animals.
OwnsPet(tom) ::: Tom is a pet owner.
Conclusion:
¬Grumpy(tom) ::: Tom is not a grumpy person.
